evidence.support: Tests withdrawal of an exemption by notification and the resulting availability of input tax credit.
The item’s exempt-to-taxable status change is relevant to the exempt-supply framework.

mappings.note: ITC on capital goods used for formerly exempt supplies becoming taxable; principal fit is the power to grant exemption and its withdrawal.

evidence.support: Determines whether lending securities for consideration is a supply of services despite securities being involved.
The analysis turns on the legal distinction between securities and services in the statutory definitions.

mappings.note: The shared stem asks whether each transaction amounts to supply; this item applies that test to securities lending.

evidence.support: Applies Schedule I to decide whether a principal-to-agent transfer without consideration is a supply.
The agent relationship and goods transfer engage statutory definitions of principal, agent and goods.
Agent status and consideration are central to determining the treatment of the uncompensated transfer.

mappings.note: The invoice issued by the agent in its own name makes the principal-agent transfer a Schedule I supply; the onward sale is also supply.

evidence.support: Tests whether payment for a promise to refrain from joining a competitor is a taxable supply of service.

mappings.note: The payment is for forbearance outside the employment relationship, so it is treated as supply under GST.
Concerns remission or refund of customs duty on imported goods destroyed before clearance or while warehoused; no candidate describes customs duty remission or refund.
